title: Finite-trial bands widened third-order half-loss bounds in two selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested finite-trial uncertainty in weighted contact failure models for two published mouse contact sets. At 10,000 ideal trials per connection, simultaneous binomial bands for all moments through order three gave mean sharp half-weight-loss range widths of 0.020131 in 1,512 Allen V1DD connections and 0.020706 in 1,438 MICrONS connections. Exact third-order widths were 0.000579 and 0.000976. Adding triples to the same finite-trial pair bands reduced width by about 32 percent in both sets. A separate ideal-count direct-event estimate gave mean interval widths of 0.008160 and 0.008296. All 2,240 endpoint certificates passed an independent audit. Exact references matched prior results and a second run reproduced aggregates. Counts are fixed design inputs, not observed trials or expected interval widths. Rates, size weights and trial independence are assumed. One animal per map and no release or activity measurements prevent biological reliability claims. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External contact records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Mean probability range widths in two ideal-count designs. All moment orders have finite-trial bands. Pair and third share a multiplicity budget. Direct uses a separate single-event interval. The figure does not show observed trials or animal confidence intervals.
